import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I’ll trace how notification tabs are rendered and how `,n` selects Gates, then use the `/sase_plan` skill to write, validate, and submit a plan before changing files.

I’m also using `/sase_memory_read` to load the TUI and plan-sizing guidance before choosing the scope of the fix.

I found a likely common cause: both the notification modal and `,n` read only the first 100 unread notifications. If an older gate falls outside that slice, the modal loses its Gates tab and `,n` cannot find the notification.

There is also a four-chip limit in the top-bar indicator, but that is separate from the modal. I’m checking the data path and reproducing the 100-row failure before settling the plan.

The reproduction confirms it: with 99 newer notifications, Gates appears and the agent shortcut opens the plan; with 100 newer notifications, Gates disappears and the shortcut does nothing. The provider silently drops the older rows and reports neither truncation nor a continuation cursor.

I’m choosing a medium-sized tale plan to remove the default row cutoff and add regression coverage through the provider, modal, and agent shortcut. The existing indicator chip limit can remain independent of notification access.

The plan is written. It covers complete reads by default, accurate metadata for explicitly limited reads, and tests for older gates and other tabs—including a real `,n` keypress test.

The first validation found a missing title field. I’ve added it and am revalidating before submission. Application files remain unchanged.

The medium tale plan passes validation with zero warnings. I’m submitting it with `sase plan propose` now, as requested, to hand it to SASE’s review flow before implementation.

The confirmed defect is the silent 100-notification cutoff shared by the modal and `,n`. No application files have been changed.
